stage_and_resources.state: The admission process retains local identities; the new process updates them, reads rows/history, then destroys logical resources. Simulator data can remain under ignored .alchemy.

inputs: Migration 001_create.sql creates storage_probe(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, version INTEGER NOT NULL, value TEXT NOT NULL).
Migration 002_marker.sql adds marker TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT migration-2. Both files applied to fresh storage, not a populated version upgrade.
One row per store, an intentional update failure, and 16 conditional UPDATE WHERE version = 0 RETURNING version attempts.
Same synthetic agent fixture as alchemy-native-agent/001; new runtime execution and recorded timestamps.
procedure: Use the exact as-run archive and unchanged upstream pinned/ patched dependency graph. Follow commands.txt; root combined scripts also invoke the separate Kit probe.
Deploy local native D1 Database with two migration files and native STORAGE Durable Object using SqlMigrations. Insert and read a controlled row in each.

In the Durable Object, update inside a transaction and yield a tagged RollbackProbe failure. In D1, batch an update with an intentional duplicate-primary-key insert. Assert each row and history match the snapshot before failure.
Issue 16 concurrent conditional updates per store. Assert exactly one winner, one final row at version 1 and unchanged two-entry migration history. Reapply the same Durable Object migrations.
Close the first runtime scope while retaining local identities. In a new Bun/workerd process, read both stores and assert exact row/history equality, then destroy local resources.
The same test processes rerun native agent callback completion and duplicate-admission checks. Later native bundle/readiness/destroy passes separately.
expected_result: Both native local storage bindings initialize two migrations, preserve pre-failure data/history under their supported rollback operation, admit one of 16 conditional writes, and return exactly the same final row/history in a new runtime process. Local cleanup succeeds.

observed_result.scope: Local native Alchemy Durable Object SQLite and native D1 migration initialization, forced rollback, finite conditional-update contention and clean process restart.
observed_result.migration_scope: Two ordered migrations applied to fresh storage; no populated v1-to-v2 live upgrade tested. Durable Object reapplies the same captured migrations; D1 is a no-op resource on restart.

rollback_semantics.durable: state.storage.transaction updates the row then fails with Schema-tagged RollbackProbe; row/history match the pre-transaction snapshot.
rollback_semantics.d1: SQL.D1 batch updates the row then inserts an existing primary key; typed SqlError retains UNIQUE constraint cause, and the full batch rolls back.
rollback_semantics.d1_interactive_transactions: Not tested by this run; installed @effect/sql-d14.0.0 rejects interactive transaction acquisition. Only atomic batches are claimed.

observed_result.concurrency_scope: 16 Effect fibers issued conditional UPDATE ... WHERE version = 0 RETURNING version in one local run per store; exactly one winner each. This is not distributed or adversarial contention coverage.
